login.changeRequiredBody: You are using a temporary password. Set a personal password to continue.
login.passwordsDoNotMatch: The two passwords do not match.
login.subtitle: Sign in to browse and administer artifacts.

browser.dockerfileReconstructed: Reconstructed from the image history — instructions are faithful, ARG values and comments are not.
browser.noDockerfile: No Dockerfile available for this image.
browser.noRoute: No reachable route — give this registry (or a group containing it) a host or a port.
browser.selectRepo: Select a repository on the left to see its tags.

explorer.noArtifacts: No artifacts in this registry yet.
explorer.title: Explorer

apikeys.createdTitle: API key created — copy it now
apikeys.empty: No keys yet. Create one for each service or script.
apikeys.intro: Keys authenticate as you: as a client password (docker login -u your-name) and as a bearer token for the API. Optional restrictions narrow the key; every request must still pass your own grants, so a key can never exceed you.
apikeys.revokeMessage: Revoking a key immediately blocks its access. Services using it stop working.
apikeys.signinRequiredBody: API keys belong to a named account. Anonymous callers have no account to own one with.
apikeys.title: API keys

grants.anonBody: A role holding administrative permissions is refused here. Anonymous access is for reading, and typically for image pulls from inside the cluster.
grants.empty: No grant yet — nobody can do anything.
grants.intro: A grant is what makes a role take effect: it ties one to somebody, within a scope. Nothing is permitted without one.
grants.removeMessage: Remove {{role}} from {{subject}}? If it is the last one that leaves somebody able to administer, the change is refused and nothing is lost.
grants.title: Grants

grantsEditor.empty: No restrictions — the key carries the owner's full power.
grantsEditor.title: Restrictions

scope.patternDesc: * covers one path segment, ** any number. kosmos/** means the repositories under kosmos/, not one named kosmos.

secrets.nameDesc: How you will refer to it elsewhere. Give it a name you will recognise in six months.
secrets.nameValueRequired: Name and value are both required.
secrets.valueDesc: Stored encrypted. It cannot be read back afterwards — only replaced.

stores.connectionDesc: Carries the account key, so it is always stored as a credential.
stores.credentialsBody: Access keys and connection strings are held encrypted and referenced by name, so one credential can serve several stores and rotating it is a single edit. A stored value is never shown again — it can be replaced, not read.
stores.deleteMessage: Delete {{name}}? The stored objects are not removed — only this definition.
stores.deleteUsedMessage: {{name}} is used by {{users}}. Detach those registries first.
stores.descriptionPlaceholder: What this backend is, in a few words
stores.empty: No store yet. Create one before adding a registry — a registry needs somewhere to put its blobs.
stores.fileNote: A filesystem store lives on one node. Every registry using it is pinned there, and follows that node down.
stores.needName: Give the store a name first.
stores.secretKeyDesc: Leave the credential unset to use the ambient AWS credential chain instead.
stores.sharedNote: Several registries can share one store. Each is given its own namespace inside it automatically, so they never overwrite or delete each other's data — there is no path to set here.
stores.title: Blob stores

registries.basePathDesc: URL prefix on the virtual hosts above, e.g. maven-central serves https://host/maven-central/…. The longest matching prefix wins; empty keeps the legacy catch-all.
registries.cacheBody: Acts as a transparent mirror: every pull is served from the local store and, on a miss, fetched from the upstream resolved by the repo host (host-less repos use the default upstream). Writes are rejected. Point containerd mirrors at this registry.
registries.defaultUpstreamLabel: Default upstream (host-less repos, e.g. Docker Hub)
registries.deleteKeyPrompt: Delete the signing key of "{{name}}"? Releases go back to unsigned.
registries.gcIntro: Reaps blobs no manifest links and no artifact object embeds. Blobs younger than the grace period are never candidates, which keeps pushes still in flight out of the sweep. Preview first, then run.
registries.groupNeedsMember: A group needs at least one member registry.
registries.membersDesc: Reads are served by the first member that has the repository; order matters. Deselect and reselect to reorder.
registries.noSigningKey: No signing key — Release is served unsigned.
registries.pointApt: Point apt at the signed metadata:
registries.saveFirstSigning: Save the registry first, then generate a signing key.
registries.storeNote: The registry gets its own namespace inside the store automatically, so several registries can share one backend safely.
registries.title: Registries
registries.warmPrompt: Warm image into this cache (e.g. gcr.io/x/y:v1):

roles.adminHint: Always global: a grant cannot narrow these to one registry.
roles.builtInTip: Built in: it holds every permission, including ones added in future releases, and cannot be changed or deleted.
roles.deleteMessage: Delete {{name}}? Every grant using it is removed too.
roles.descriptionPlaceholder: What someone holding this role is meant to do
roles.intro: A role is a set of permissions. It grants nothing on its own — it takes effect when a grant ties it to someone within a scope.
roles.registryHint: Apply wherever the grant using this role points.
roles.title: Roles

serviceAccounts.createdTitle: API key created — copy it now
serviceAccounts.revokeMessage: Revoking a service account key immediately blocks its access.
serviceAccounts.title: Service Accounts

settings.anonBodyPost: subject; grant it a role scoped to the registry under Administration → Roles and Grants to decide what anonymous clients may do.
settings.anonBodyPre: When denied (default), every request must be authenticated. When allowed, unauthenticated requests are mapped to the
settings.passwordMismatch: The two new passwords do not match.
settings.serverNote: Server configuration (PostgreSQL connection, blob store backend, authentication realms) is provided via command-line flags or a JSON config file at startup — not through the UI, by design. See the project README for details.
settings.tempPasswordBody: You are still using a temporary password. Change it to continue using the registry.
settings.title: Settings

sso.deleteMessage: Delete {{name}}? Its client secret is dropped too, and its login button disappears immediately.
sso.empty: No provider yet. Add Microsoft 365, Google, GitHub, GitLab, LinkedIn, or a generic OIDC/OAuth2/CAS endpoint.

fieldDesc.admin_group: Members of this group (or Entra object ID) become admins.
fieldDesc.base_url: Self-hosted base (GitLab) or CAS server base.
fieldDesc.entity_id: Our identifier as registered at the IdP (audience of assertions).
fieldDesc.groups_claim: Empty keeps the preset mapping (or none).
fieldDesc.idp_cert: PEM certificate the IdP signs responses with.
fieldDesc.idp_sso_url: Where browsers are sent to sign in.
fieldDesc.scope: Space-separated. Empty keeps the preset scopes.
fieldDesc.tenant: Entra directory tenant. Never use common unless any Microsoft account may sign in.

sso.idDesc: Unique handle in login URLs (a-z, 0-9, dashes).
sso.intro: Browser login buttons for the sign-in page. Providers activate immediately — no restart. Client secrets are stored encrypted and can never be read back.
sso.keepSecret: Leave empty to keep the stored secret.
sso.labelDesc: Button text on the sign-in page.
sso.title: Single sign-on

users.createHint: The account starts with no access at all. Give it a grant, or add it to a group that already has one.
users.deleteMessage: Delete {{name}}? Grants made directly to this account stop applying.
users.disabledDesc: A disabled account cannot sign in, and does not count as an administrator.
users.grantsHint: Grants are managed on the Grants page.
users.intro: An account grants nothing by itself. What someone can do comes from the grants made to them, to a group they belong to, or to everyone signed in.
users.newPasswordPlaceholder: leave empty to keep the current one
users.noAccess: No grant reaches this account. It can sign in and see nothing.
users.title: Users

groups.deleteMessage: Delete {{name}}? Grants made to it are removed too, so its members lose whatever they reached through it.
groups.intro: Grant a role to a group and it reaches every member. Identities arriving from LDAP or OIDC bring their own groups as claims; these are for local accounts, and both resolve the same way.
groups.membersDesc: Local accounts. Federated identities join through their own group claims.
groups.title: Groups

credentials.deleteMessage: Delete {{key}}? The value is gone for good.
credentials.deleteUsedMessage: {{key}} is used by {{users}}. Detach it there first — the server refuses the deletion.
credentials.intro: Stored encrypted and referenced by name, so one credential can serve several stores and rotating it is a single edit. A value goes in once and is never shown again — it can be replaced, not read.
credentials.inUseBody: {{names}} will start using the new value at once. Make sure it is already valid at the provider.
credentials.nameDesc: How you will refer to it elsewhere. Pick something you will recognise in six months.
credentials.rotateHint: Everything referencing this credential picks up the new value immediately. That is the point of naming credentials instead of copying them.
credentials.secretDesc: Encrypted at rest. It cannot be read back afterwards.
credentials.title: Credentials

anonymous.addressesDesc: One CIDR per line. Leave empty to accept any address — that makes this a catch-all, and it is tried after every restricted identity.
anonymous.catchAllBody: {{names}} all accept any address. Only the first is ever reached.
anonymous.createHint: An identity grants nothing on its own. After creating it, give it a grant — typically a read-only role scoped to the registries it should pull from.
anonymous.deleteMessage: Delete {{name}}? Callers it used to recognise fall through to the next matching identity, or are refused if there is none.
anonymous.descriptionPlaceholder: Image pulls from the cluster nodes
anonymous.empty: No anonymous identity. Callers without credentials are refused.
anonymous.intro: A caller with no credentials is matched against these in order, and the first that fits becomes the principal. From then on it is treated like any other identity: what it may do comes from the grants made to it. Address-restricted identities are tried first, so a catch-all never hides a narrower rule.
anonymous.nameDesc: Grants are made to this name, the same way as for a user.
anonymous.proxyBodyPost: is set to match the number of proxies in front of the registry, a CIDR rule cannot tell an outside caller from an in-cluster one. Reading the header without that would be worse: anyone could claim any address.
anonymous.proxyBodyPre: No proxy hop is trusted, so the address seen is the one the connection came from — for traffic through the gateway that is the gateway itself, not the caller. Until
anonymous.proxyTitle: Address filters are not being applied as you expect
anonymous.title: Anonymous access
